methodology.deduplication: One canonical record per distinct layoff event; corroborating source URLs are retained in the event record.
methodology.headcount: Only numeric figures with a source are included in aggregate headcounts. Undisclosed counts are excluded.
methodology.dates: event_date records when the workforce action was announced or took effect, as explicitly described by sources; publication dates belong to individual source records.
methodology.initial_population_note: Initial population includes Enphase Energy and Skyscanner records verified in the immediately preceding research cycle but not yet published, plus the Oracle European Works Council proposal discovered during catch-up research. The Oracle figure is an unverified reported maximum, not confirmed completed layoffs.
methodology.ai_attribution: Following the Layoffs.fyi AI tracker scope, include events attributed to AI by the company or credible press: to fund AI investment, replace human work with AI, or respond to AI-driven market disruption. Preserve attribution status; press attribution is not company confirmation.
methodology.benchmark_attribution: Layoffs.fyi is linked as an external benchmark with attribution. Fired records remain independently normalized and source-linked; benchmark totals are not merged into Fired aggregates.

events.headline: SAP reportedly weighs at least 10,000 potential job cuts in an AI-era restructuring
events.event_date_note: First public reporting date of the proposal; implementation date and final decision date have not been disclosed.
events.geography_note: Global workforce; country-level allocation has not been disclosed. SAP is headquartered in Walldorf, Germany. Its German labour council negotiated an employment guarantee through 2028.
events.figure_note: Bloomberg reports that SAP is preparing a plan involving at least 10,000 positions, equivalent to at least 9% of its global workforce. The number is not final and may change after labour negotiations. SAP declined to comment on whether job cuts are planned; Reuters said it could not independently verify Bloomberg's report. The 10,000 figure is a reported minimum under consideration, not confirmed completed layoffs. Reuters separately reported on 2026-11-27, citing two people familiar with the matter, that SAP is preparing to cut a sizeable number of jobs and that the works council had not yet been informed; this follow-up did not quantify the cuts or independently confirm Bloomberg's at-least-10,000 figure.
events.company_response_note: SAP said it continuously reviews its organisation to remain aligned with strategy and customer needs, and declined to comment on whether any job cuts are planned.

events.headline: Swiggy's Instamart reportedly cuts around 340 corporate and support roles amid restructuring
events.event_date_note: Date of the newly reported workforce action. Exact employee notification and last-working dates have not been disclosed; coverage varies between 'set to lay off' and 'has laid off'.
events.geography_note: Instamart corporate and support functions; city- or office-level allocation not disclosed. Swiggy is headquartered in Bengaluru, India.
events.percentage_basis_note: Financial Express calculates approximately 3.8% against Swiggy's 9,047 employees as of March 31, 2026. This is a Swiggy-wide denominator, not an Instamart-only workforce percentage; 303 contractual staff are separately reported.
events.figure_note: Approximately 340 Instamart roles are reported by Moneycontrol, The Economic Times, Financial Express, Reuters and other outlets. Reuters separately cited a person familiar with the matter who said Swiggy would cut 340 roles; Swiggy did not respond to Reuters' request for comment. The figure remains reported, not a company-confirmed disclosure.
events.company_response_note: Moneycontrol said Swiggy did not immediately reply to its queries; Inc42 said Swiggy declined to comment; Reuters also reported that Swiggy did not respond to its request for comment. No company-confirmed headcount was located.
